title.en: subject and object questions · indirect questions: Could you tell me…? · question tags

summary.es: subject and object questions · indirect questions: Could you tell me…? · question tags

explanation.es:
Preguntas de sujeto y de objeto

Si la palabra interrogativa es el objeto, usamos auxiliar (do/does/did). Si es el sujeto, no:

Pregunta de objetoPregunta de sujeto
Who did you call? (Llamaste a alguien: ¿a quién?)Who called you? (Alguien te llamó: ¿quién?)
What did she say?What happened?
Which team do you support?Which team won?
✗ What did happen? → ✓ What happened? · ✗ Who did write this? → ✓ Who wrote this?

Preguntas indirectas

Son más educadas. Tras la introducción, el orden es el de una frase afirmativa y desaparece do/does/did:

DirectaIndirecta
Where is the station?Could you tell me where the station is?
What time does it open?Do you know what time it opens?
Is she coming?I wonder if / whether she's coming.

Question tags

Pequeñas preguntas al final para confirmar («¿verdad?», «¿no?»). Afirmativa → tag negativo y al revés, con el mismo auxiliar:

You're Spanish, aren't you? · She lives here, doesn't she? · They didn't come, did they? · You can swim, can't you? · I'm late, aren't I?

examples.en: Who broke the window? — Tom did.
examples.es: ¿Quién rompió la ventana? —Tom.

examples.en: Could you tell me where the toilets are ?
examples.es: ¿Podría decirme dónde están los servicios?

examples.en: You live near here, don't you?
examples.es: Vives cerca de aquí, ¿no?

examples.en: I wonder if she'll come to the party.
examples.es: Me pregunto si vendrá a la fiesta.

examples.en: Who did you meet at the party?
examples.es: ¿A quién conociste en la fiesta?

examples.en: She hasn't finished yet, has she?
examples.es: Todavía no ha terminado, ¿verdad?

title.en: past perfect: had + participle · narrative tenses · by the time, before, after, already

summary.es: past perfect: had + participle · narrative tenses · by the time, before, after, already

explanation.es:
El pasado perfecto

had + participio. Se usa para dejar claro que algo ocurrió antes de otro momento del pasado:

When I got to the station, the train had left. (primero se fue el tren, luego llegué yo)
She was nervous because she had never flown before.
Pasado simplePasado perfecto
When we arrived, they started eating. (llegamos → empezaron)When we arrived, they had started eating. (ya habían empezado)

Los tres tiempos narrativos juntos

pasado continuoel fondo, la escenaIt was raining and people were hurrying home.
pasado simplelos hechos principales, en ordenSuddenly a man ran out of the bank.
pasado perfectolo que había pasado antesHe had stolen €10,000.
Expresiones típicas: by the time (para cuando), already (ya), before, after, as soon as, until. Con after y before el orden ya está claro y se puede usar pasado simple: After he (had) finished, he left.
El español también tiene «había + participio», así que el uso es muy parecido. El error típico es en la forma: ✗ When I arrived, the film has started → ✓ had started.

examples.en: When I got home, someone had broken into my flat.
examples.es: Cuando llegué a casa, alguien había entrado a robar en mi piso.

examples.en: I had seen that film before, so I didn't go.
examples.es: Ya había visto esa película, así que no fui.

examples.en: While she was walking in the park, she found a wallet.
examples.es: Mientras paseaba por el parque, encontró una cartera.

examples.en: By the time the police arrived, the thief had escaped .
examples.es: Para cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón se había escapado.

examples.en: We had never seen such a beautiful place.
examples.es: Nunca habíamos visto un sitio tan bonito.

examples.en: The film had already started when we arrived.
examples.es: La película ya había empezado cuando llegamos.

title.en: used to / didn't use to · would for past habits · be used to / get used to

summary.es: used to / didn't use to · would for past habits · be used to / get used to

explanation.es:
used to

Hábitos y estados del pasado que ya no son así. Equivale a «solía» o al imperfecto español:

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I used to live in Seville.I didn't use to like vegetables.Did you use to play outside?
Con didn't y did se escribe use to (sin -d). Para un hábito presente no existe use to: «suelo levantarme temprano» = I usually get up early (✗ I use to get up).

would para hábitos del pasado

En narraciones, would también expresa acciones repetidas del pasado, pero no estados:

Every summer we would go to the beach and my grandfather would tell us stories. ✓
✗ We would live in a small house. → ✓ We used to live in a small house. (estado)

be used to / get used to + -ing

be used to + -ing / sustantivoestar acostumbrado aI'm used to getting up early.
get used to + -ing / sustantivoacostumbrarse aI can't get used to the cold.
No confundas: I used to drive (antes conducía) / I'm used to driving (estoy acostumbrado a conducir).

examples.en: I used to play the piano when I was a child.
examples.es: De niño tocaba el piano.

examples.en: Did you use to wear a uniform at school?
examples.es: ¿Llevabas uniforme en el colegio?

examples.en: Now I live in London, but I'm not used to driving on the left.
examples.es: Ahora vivo en Londres, pero no estoy acostumbrado a conducir por la izquierda.

examples.en: Every Sunday my grandmother would make a big lunch for everyone.
examples.es: Todos los domingos mi abuela preparaba una gran comida para todos.

examples.en: We used to spend every summer at the beach.
examples.es: Pasábamos todos los veranos en la playa.

examples.en: It took me a long time to get used to the weather.
examples.es: Me costó mucho acostumbrarme al clima.

title.en: present perfect vs past simple · ever, never, so far, recently · been vs gone

summary.es: present perfect vs past simple · ever, never, so far, recently · been vs gone

explanation.es:
¿Present perfect o pasado simple?

Present perfect (have/has + participio)Pasado simple
El momento no se dice o no importa; periodo que llega hasta ahoraMomento terminado y concreto
I've been to Japan three times.I went to Japan in 2019.
She's won two medals this year.She won a medal last year.
ever, never, yet, already, just, so far, recently, this week, todayyesterday, last…, … ago, in 2010, when I was young
Truco: si puedes preguntar When? y la respuesta está en la frase, usa pasado simple. Las preguntas con When van siempre en pasado simple: ✓ When did you arrive? (✗ When have you arrived?).
Diferencias con el español peninsular: «Hoy he visto a Juan» = I've seen Juan today (igual). Pero «Esta mañana he ido al médico», dicho por la tarde = This morning I went to the doctor (la mañana ya terminó). Y en la biografía de alguien que ha muerto, siempre pasado simple: Picasso painted many pictures.
— Have you ever run a marathon? — Yes, I have. I ran the Valencia marathon last year. It took me four hours.

examples.en: I 've lost my keys. Can you help me look for them?
examples.es: He perdido las llaves. ¿Me ayudas a buscarlas?

examples.en: We went to Paris in 2018.
examples.es: Fuimos a París en 2018.

examples.en: So far, she has won three races this season.
examples.es: Hasta ahora ha ganado tres carreras esta temporada.

examples.en: When did you start working here?
examples.es: ¿Cuándo empezaste a trabajar aquí?

examples.en: She has achieved a lot in her career.
examples.es: Ha logrado mucho en su carrera.

examples.en: I haven't seen him since last summer.
examples.es: No lo he visto desde el verano pasado.

title.en: present perfect continuous: have been + -ing · for / since · How long…?

summary.es: present perfect continuous: have been + -ing · for / since · How long…?

explanation.es:
Present perfect continuo

have / has been + -ing. Para una actividad que empezó en el pasado y continúa (o acaba de terminar), con énfasis en la duración:

I've been learning English for three years. (llevo tres años aprendiendo)
It's been raining since this morning.
How long have you been waiting? — For about twenty minutes.
You look tired. — I've been running. (acabo de parar; se nota el resultado)
El español usa presente o «llevar + gerundio»: «Vivo aquí desde 2015», «Llevo dos horas esperando». El inglés no admite presente: ✗ I live here since 2015 → ✓ I've lived / I've been living here since 2015.

for y since

for + periodofor two hours, for ages, for a long time
since + punto de partidasince 2010, since Monday, since I was a child

¿Simple o continuo?

Present perfect simplePresent perfect continuo
resultado, cantidad terminadaactividad, duración
I've read three books this month.I've been reading all afternoon.
verbos de estado: I've known her for years.✗ I've been knowing her

examples.en: I've been waiting for an hour!
examples.es: ¡Llevo una hora esperando!

examples.en: She's been working here since 2019.
examples.es: Trabaja aquí desde 2019.

examples.en: How long have you been learning Japanese?
examples.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas estudiando japonés?

examples.en: I've known her since we were at school.
examples.es: La conozco desde que íbamos al colegio.

examples.en: It has been raining all day.
examples.es: Ha estado lloviendo todo el día.

examples.en: How long have you been living here?
examples.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas viviendo aquí?

title.en: will / going to / present continuous · might / may · be likely to, definitely, probably

summary.es: will / going to / present continuous · might / may · be likely to, definitely, probably

explanation.es:
Repaso de las formas de futuro

FormaUsoEjemplo
present continuousplan organizado (fecha, entradas…)I'm flying to Berlin on Friday.
be going tointención; predicción con pruebasI'm going to look for a new job.
willpredicción, decisión en el momento, promesaYou'll love it. I'll call you.
present simplehorarios y programasThe train leaves at 7.15.

Probabilidad

100%I will definitely come. / I'm certain to…
80%I'll probably come. / I'm likely to come.
50%I might / may come. (puede que vaya)
20%I probably won't come. / I'm unlikely to come.
0%I definitely won't come.
might / may + forma base, sin to: It might rain (✗ it might to rain, ✗ it mights). Posición de los adverbios: She'll probably pass, pero She probably won't pass.
«Puede que llueva» no es «can»: ✗ It can rain tomorrow → ✓ It might / may rain tomorrow.

examples.en: Take an umbrella. It might rain later.
examples.es: Llévate un paraguas. Puede que llueva más tarde.

examples.en: The film starts at 8.30, so let's meet at 8.
examples.es: La película empieza a las 8.30, así que quedamos a las 8.

examples.en: She's very ill. She won't probably come to work tomorrow.
examples.es: Está muy enferma. Probablemente no venga a trabajar mañana.

examples.en: Prices are likely to rise next year.
examples.es: Es probable que los precios suban el año que viene.

examples.en: We're having a party on Saturday night.
examples.es: El sábado por la noche damos una fiesta.

examples.en: I don't think he'll get the job.
examples.es: No creo que consiga el trabajo.

title.en: zero and first conditional · second conditional: if + past, would · If I were you…

summary.es: zero and first conditional · second conditional: if + past, would · If I were you…

explanation.es:
Condicional cero y primero (repaso)

cero: verdades generalesIf you heat water to 100°, it boils.
primero: situaciones reales y posiblesIf it rains, we'll stay at home.

Segundo condicional

Para situaciones imaginarias, improbables o contrarias a la realidad en el presente o el futuro:

if + pasado simplewould + verbo
If I won the lottery,I'd travel around the world.
If she had more time,she'd learn Japanese.
If I were you,I'd accept the job.
Es el «si tuviera…, viajaría» del español: el inglés usa el pasado simple donde el español usa el imperfecto de subjuntivo. Con be se prefiere were para todas las personas (If I were you), aunque en lenguaje coloquial se oye was.

¿Primero o segundo?

If I get the job, I'll buy a car. (es posible: me han entrevistado)
If I got the job, I'd buy a car. (lo veo poco probable)
Nunca would después de if: ✗ If I would have money → ✓ If I had money. 'd puede ser would o had: I'd go = I would go.

examples.en: If I had a lot of money, I'd buy a house by the sea.
examples.es: Si tuviera mucho dinero, me compraría una casa junto al mar.

examples.en: If I were you, I 'd talk to her.
examples.es: Yo que tú, hablaría con ella.

examples.en: What would you do if you were invisible?
examples.es: ¿Qué harías si fueras invisible?

examples.en: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
examples.es: Si mezclas azul y amarillo, sale verde.

examples.en: If I lived near the sea, I would go swimming every day.
examples.es: Si viviera cerca del mar, iría a nadar todos los días.

examples.en: What would you do if you lost your job?
examples.es: ¿Qué harías si perdieras el trabajo?

title.en: third conditional: if + past perfect, would have · I wish / If only + past simple / past perfect

summary.es: third conditional: if + past perfect, would have · I wish / If only + past simple / past perfect

explanation.es:
Tercer condicional

Situaciones imaginarias del pasado: algo que no pasó y sus consecuencias. Suele expresar arrepentimiento o alivio:

if + pasado perfectowould have + participio
If I had studied,I would have passed.
If you hadn't called me,I would have missed the flight.
Es el «si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado». Contracciones: If I'd known, I'd have come (el primer 'd = had, el segundo = would). En la conversación would have suena /wʊdəv/.

wish / if only

Deseo sobre el presenteArrepentimiento sobre el pasado
wish + pasado simplewish + pasado perfecto
I wish I had more free time. (ojalá tuviera)I wish I had studied harder. (ojalá hubiera estudiado)
I wish I were taller.If only I hadn't said that!
✗ If I would have known → ✓ If I had known · ✗ I wish I have a car → ✓ I wish I had a car. Para quejarse de lo que otro hace: I wish you would stop talking!

examples.en: If I had known about the party, I would have gone.
examples.es: Si hubiera sabido lo de la fiesta, habría ido.

examples.en: If she hadn't missed the bus, she wouldn't have been late.
examples.es: Si no hubiera perdido el autobús, no habría llegado tarde.

examples.en: I wish I could speak Chinese.
examples.es: Ojalá supiera hablar chino.

examples.en: I wish I hadn't said that. It was a mistake.
examples.es: Ojalá no hubiera dicho eso. Fue un error.

examples.en: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
examples.es: Si hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos cogido el tren.

examples.en: I wish I had more time to read.
examples.es: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo para leer.

title.en: must / have to / need to / don't need to · be allowed to / can · should / ought to / had better

summary.es: must / have to / need to / don't need to · be allowed to / can · should / ought to / had better

explanation.es:
Obligación y necesidad

mustobligación que siente el hablante; normas escritasI must finish this today.
have toobligación externaWe have to wear a uniform.
need tonecesidadYou need to renew your passport.
don't have to / don't need to / needn'tno es necesarioYou don't need to print it.
mustn't / can'tprohibiciónYou mustn't use your phone in meetings.

Permiso: be allowed to

Are we allowed to work from home? — Yes, we're allowed to work from home on Fridays.
We weren't allowed to leave early. (pasado)
can y must no tienen todas las formas; para otros tiempos usa be allowed to y have to: I'll have to work late. She's had to cancel. You won't be allowed to enter.

Consejo: should, ought to, had better

You should / ought to ask for a pay rise. (deberías)
You'd better hurry or you'll miss the deadline. (más vale que… — advertencia)
had better + forma base, sin to: ✗ You'd better to go. Negativa: You'd better not be late.ought to sí lleva to.

examples.en: Employees are not allowed to smoke in the building.
examples.es: Los empleados no pueden fumar en el edificio.

examples.en: You don't need to bring your laptop. We have computers here.
examples.es: No hace falta que traigas el portátil. Aquí tenemos ordenadores.

examples.en: You'd better not be late for the interview.
examples.es: Más vale que no llegues tarde a la entrevista.

examples.en: Next year we'll have to work on Saturdays.
examples.es: El año que viene tendremos que trabajar los sábados.

examples.en: Do we have to wear a suit to the meeting?
examples.es: ¿Tenemos que llevar traje a la reunión?

examples.en: You should ask for more information.
examples.es: Deberías pedir más información.

title.en: modals of deduction: must, might, may, could, can't · look / seem / sound like

summary.es: modals of deduction: must, might, may, could, can't · look / seem / sound like

explanation.es:
Deducir con modales

Grado de certezaModalEjemplo
casi seguro que símustThe lights are on. They must be at home.
posiblemight / may / couldShe might be ill. It could be a mistake.
casi seguro que nocan'tThat can't be Tom. He's in Japan.
Lo contrario de must en deducciones es can't, no mustn't: ✗ He mustn't be hungry; he's just eaten → ✓ He can't be hungry. Para algo en curso: must be + -ing: She isn't answering. She must be driving.

Parece que…

He looks tired. (adjetivo)Parece cansado (por su aspecto).
It looks like rain. / It looks like a cat. (sustantivo)Parece que va a llover. / Parece un gato.
You sound happy. That sounds like a great idea.Pareces contento (por la voz). Parece una gran idea.
She seems nice. It seems that nobody knows.Parece simpática. Parece que nadie lo sabe.
En español «deber de» expresa deducción (debe de estar en casa) y «deber» obligación; el inglés usa must para las dos, y el contexto decide.

examples.en: She's not answering her phone. She must be asleep.
examples.es: No contesta al teléfono. Debe de estar dormida.

examples.en: That can't be Anna's car. She sold it last year.
examples.es: Ese no puede ser el coche de Anna. Lo vendió el año pasado.

examples.en: I'm not sure where Tom is. He might be in the library.
examples.es: No sé dónde está Tom. Puede que esté en la biblioteca.

examples.en: You look as if you haven't slept for days!
examples.es: ¡Parece que no hayas dormido en días!

examples.en: They must be on holiday.
examples.es: Deben de estar de vacaciones.

examples.en: It might be a good idea to call first.
examples.es: Quizá sería buena idea llamar primero.

title.en: passive: be + past participle · by + agent · present, past, present perfect and future passive

summary.es: passive: be + past participle · by + agent · present, past, present perfect and future passive

explanation.es:
La pasiva

be + participio. Se usa cuando importa la acción o el objeto, no quién lo hace (o no se sabe):

TiempoActivaPasiva
presenteThey make cars here.Cars are made here.
pasadoSomeone stole my bike.My bike was stolen.
present perfectThey have opened a new shop.A new shop has been opened.
futuroThey will finish the bridge next year.The bridge will be finished next year.
presente continuoThey are repairing the road.The road is being repaired.
con modalYou must sign the form.The form must be signed.
Guernicawas painted by Picasso in 1937. (by = quién lo hizo)
Coffee is grown in Colombia. · English is spoken all over the world.
El español usa mucho la pasiva refleja con se: «Aquí se habla inglés», «Se vende piso». En inglés: English is spoken here, Flat for sale. «Se dice que…» = It is said that…
✗ The bridge was build in 1890 → ✓ was built (participio) · ✗ It was happened → ✓ It happened (los verbos intransitivos no tienen pasiva).

examples.en: This bridge was built in 1890.
examples.es: Este puente se construyó en 1890.

examples.en: Spanish is spoken in more than twenty countries.
examples.es: El español se habla en más de veinte países.

examples.en: The road is being repaired, so we have to take another way.
examples.es: Están arreglando la carretera, así que tenemos que ir por otro camino.

examples.en: The winners will be announced tomorrow.
examples.es: Los ganadores se anunciarán mañana.

examples.en: These shoes are made in Italy.
examples.es: Estos zapatos están hechos en Italia.

examples.en: The museum has been closed for repairs.
examples.es: El museo está cerrado por obras.

title.en: reported speech: statements · reported questions · say vs tell · ask / tell someone to

summary.es: reported speech: statements · reported questions · say vs tell · ask / tell someone to

explanation.es:
Estilo indirecto: los tiempos «retroceden»

Si el verbo introductor está en pasado (said, told), el verbo de lo dicho suele ir un tiempo atrás:

Estilo directoEstilo indirecto
"I am tired."She said (that) she was tired.
"I work in a bank."He said he worked in a bank.
"I saw the film."She said she had seen the film.
"I'll call you."He said he would call me.
"I can help."She said she could help.
Cambian también pronombres y referencias de tiempo y lugar: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there, this → that.

say y tell

say (something) (to someone)She said (to me) that she was busy.
tell + personaShe told me that she was busy.

Preguntas y órdenes en estilo indirecto

"Where do you live?" → He asked me where I lived. (orden afirmativo, sin do)
"Are you OK?" → She asked if / whether I was OK.
"Sit down." → He told me to sit down. · "Don't shout." → She asked us not to shout.
✗ He said me → ✓ He told me / He said to me · ✗ She asked me where did I live → ✓ where I lived.

examples.en: She told me that she was moving to Canada.
examples.es: Me dijo que se mudaba a Canadá.

examples.en: He said he would call me later, but he didn't.
examples.es: Dijo que me llamaría más tarde, pero no lo hizo.

examples.en: They asked me where I was from.
examples.es: Me preguntaron de dónde era.

examples.en: The doctor told me to stop smoking.
examples.es: El médico me dijo que dejara de fumar.

examples.en: She asked me to close the window.
examples.es: Me pidió que cerrara la ventana.

examples.en: He told us that he had lost his passport.
examples.es: Nos dijo que había perdido el pasaporte.

title.en: defining relative clauses · non-defining relative clauses (with commas) · who, which, whose, where, when

summary.es: defining relative clauses · non-defining relative clauses (with commas) · who, which, whose, where, when

explanation.es:
Especificativas y explicativas

Especificativas (defining)Explicativas (non-defining)
Información necesaria para saber de quién hablamosInformación extra, entre comas
The man who lives next door is a doctor.My neighbour, who is a doctor, works nights.
Se puede usar thatNunca that
Se puede omitir el pronombre objeto: the book (that) I readNo se omite nada
Madrid, which is the capital of Spain, has about 3.3 million inhabitants.
My sister, whose husband is Irish, lives in Dublin.
I'll never forget the day when I met her.
This is the café where we first met.
which también puede referirse a toda una frase (como «lo cual»): He passed the exam, which surprised everyone. En registro formal: the person to whom I spoke; en conversación: the person I spoke to.
✗ My brother, that lives in Paris, … → ✓ My brother, who lives in Paris, … · ✗ What I want is the red one — aquí what = lo que (✓); pero ✗ the thing what I want → ✓ the thing that I want.

examples.en: My grandmother, who is 90, still drives.
examples.es: Mi abuela, que tiene 90 años, todavía conduce.

examples.en: The town where I grew up has changed a lot.
examples.es: El pueblo donde me crié ha cambiado mucho.

examples.en: He failed the exam, which was a big surprise.
examples.es: Suspendió el examen, lo cual fue una gran sorpresa.

examples.en: That's the architect whose buildings are famous all over the world.
examples.es: Ese es el arquitecto cuyos edificios son famosos en todo el mundo.

examples.en: This is the hotel where we stayed last year.
examples.es: Este es el hotel donde nos alojamos el año pasado.

examples.en: I remember the day when we first met.
examples.es: Recuerdo el día en que nos conocimos.

title.en: verb + -ing / verb + to · remember, forget, stop, try + -ing or to · -ing as subject; after prepositions

summary.es: verb + -ing / verb + to · remember, forget, stop, try + -ing or to · -ing as subject; after prepositions

explanation.es:
Verbo + -ing

avoid, consider, deny, enjoy, finish, imagine, involve, keep, mind, miss, practise, risk, suggest, can't stand, don't mind, feel like, look forward to
I avoid driving at night. She suggested going to the cinema. I feel like having a pizza.

Verbo + to + infinitivo

afford, agree, arrange, attempt, decide, expect, fail, hope, manage, offer, plan, pretend, promise, refuse, seem, tend, want, would like
We can't afford to buy a house. He pretended to be ill.

Cambian de significado

remember to doacordarse de hacer (algo pendiente)Remember to lock the door.
remember doingrecordar haber hechoI remember locking it.
stop to doparar para hacerWe stopped to buy petrol.
stop doingdejar de hacerShe stopped smoking.
try to dointentar (esforzarse)I tried to open it, but I couldn't.
try doingprobar a hacer (como experimento)Try restarting the computer.
regret to tell / regret doinglamentar informar / arrepentirse deI regret saying that.
La forma -ing también funciona como sujeto (el infinitivo español): Swimming is good for you (✗ To swim is good…, poco natural). Y siempre tras preposición: interested in learning, before leaving, without saying goodbye.

examples.en: I can't afford to go on holiday this year.
examples.es: Este año no me puedo permitir irme de vacaciones.

examples.en: Would you consider working abroad?

title.en: phrasal verbs: look after, give up, find out… · separable and inseparable · object pronouns with phrasal verbs

summary.es: phrasal verbs: look after, give up, find out… · separable and inseparable · object pronouns with phrasal verbs

explanation.es:
¿Qué es un phrasal verb?

Verbo + partícula (up, off, out, on…) con un significado nuevo, a menudo imposible de adivinar:

give updejar, rendirsefind outaveriguar, enterarse
look aftercuidarrun out ofquedarse sin
take upempezar (una afición)put offaplazar
call offcancelarget overrecuperarse de
break downaveriarsework outhacer ejercicio; resolver

¿Dónde va el objeto?

SeparablesInseparables
turn on the TV / turn the TV on
turn it on (✗ turn on it)		look after the children
look after them (✗ look them after)
put on, take off, turn on/off, pick up, fill in, give up, call off…look after, look for, get over, deal with, come across…
Con un pronombre (it, them, her…) y un verbo separable, el pronombre va en medio: ✓ Put it on, ✓ Pick me up at 8; ✗ Put on it.
Los phrasal verbs son muy coloquiales; en textos formales suelen tener un equivalente latino: find out → discover, put off → postpone, call off → cancel, go on → continue. ¡Al hispanohablante le suenan más familiares los formales!

title.en: so + adjective / such (a) + noun · so … that / such … that · too / enough + to

summary.es: so + adjective / such (a) + noun · so … that / such … that · too / enough + to

explanation.es:
so y such

so + adjetivo / adverbioIt's so cold! She speaks so fast.
such (a) + (adjetivo) + sustantivoIt's such a cold day! They're such nice people.
so many / so muchThere were so many people!
The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.

too y enough + to

He's too young to drive. (demasiado joven para)
She's old enough to drive. (lo bastante mayor para)
We haven't got enough time to finish.

Adjetivos extremos

Algunos adjetivos ya son «extremos» y no admiten very; se intensifican con absolutely, totally, completely:

very cold → freezingvery hot → boilingvery hungry → starving
very tired → exhaustedvery big → hugevery funny → hilarious
very angry → furiousvery scared → terrifiedvery good → brilliant
✗ very freezing → ✓ absolutely freezing · ✗ It's a so nice day → ✓ It's such a nice day · ✗ enough old → ✓ old enough. really vale con los dos tipos: really cold, really freezing.

title.en: some-, any-, no-, every- (+ -body, -thing, -where) · both, either, neither · none of / all of

summary.es: some-, any-, no-, every- (+ -body, -thing, -where) · both, either, neither · none of / all of

explanation.es:
Pronombres indefinidos

-body / -one-thing-where
some- (afirmativas, ofrecimientos)somebodysomethingsomewhere
any- (negativas, preguntas; «cualquier»)anybodyanythinganywhere
no- (con verbo afirmativo)nobodynothingnowhere
every-everybodyeverythingeverywhere
El inglés no admite doble negación: «No vi a nadie» = ✓ I didn't see anybody o ✓ I saw nobody (✗ I didn't see nobody). Los indefinidos van con verbo en singular: Everybody is here (✗ are).

both · either · neither

both (los dos)Both my parents are teachers. I like both of them.
either (cualquiera de los dos; ninguno en negativas)You can take either bus. I don't like either of them.
neither (ninguno de los dos)Neither answer is correct. Neither of us knew.
both … and / either … or / neither … norShe speaks both French and German. Neither Tom nor Ann came.
Para mostrar acuerdo: — I'm tired. — So am I. / — I don't like it. — Neither do I (o Me neither).

title.en: although / even though / despite / in spite of / however · because / because of / so / therefore · moreover / furthermore / in addition

summary.es: although / even though / despite / in spite of / however · because / because of / so / therefore · moreover / furthermore / in addition

explanation.es:
Contraste

although / even though + fraseAlthough it was raining, we went out.
despite / in spite of + sustantivo o -ingDespite the rain, we went out. In spite of being tired, she kept working.
However, (al principio de otra frase)It was raining. However, we went out.
whereas / while (contraste entre dos cosas)I love the sea, whereas my sister prefers the mountains.
✗ Despite it was raining → ✓ Although it was raining / ✓ Despite the rain / ✓ Despite the fact that it was raining. ✗ Despite of → ✓ Despite / In spite of.

Causa y consecuencia

because + frase / because of, due to + sustantivoThe flight was cancelled because of the storm.
so (informal) / therefore, as a result, consequently (formal)Prices rose. As a result, sales fell.

Añadir y ordenar ideas

Firstly, … In addition / Moreover / Furthermore, … On the other hand, … In conclusion, …
Many sports, such as tennis and golf, … · Apart from English, she speaks Italian.
En una redacción del examen de la EOI se valora la variedad de conectores, pero úsalos con la puntuación correcta: However, y Moreover, van tras punto y llevan coma.

title.en: make vs do collocations · get = obtain, become, arrive, receive · have / get something done

summary.es: make vs do collocations · get = obtain, become, arrive, receive · have / get something done

explanation.es:
make o do

make: crear, producir, provocardo: actividades, tareas, trabajo
make a cake, a mistake, a decision, a noise, money, friends, an effort, progress, a phone call, an appointment, a complaint, suredo homework, the housework, the shopping, the washing-up, exercise, sport, business, research, a course, your best, someone a favour, damage
«Hacer» no siempre es make o do: hacer una pregunta = ask a question; hacer una foto = take a photo; hacer una fiesta = have / throw a party; hace frío = it's cold; hacer cola = queue.

Los significados de get

conseguir, obtenerI got a new job.
recibirDid you get my email?
llegarWhat time did you get home?
volverse, ponerse (+ adjetivo)It's getting dark. She got angry. get married / lost / ready / better
traer, ir a porCan you get some bread?
entender (coloquial)I don't get it.

have / get something done

Cuando otra persona hace algo por ti (normalmente pagando):

I had my hair cut yesterday. (me corté el pelo — en la peluquería)
We're getting the kitchen painted. · You should have your eyes tested.

title.en: much / far / a bit + comparative · the + comparative, the + comparative · comparative and comparative · as … as / the same as / similar to / different from

summary.es: much / far / a bit + comparative · the + comparative, the + comparative · comparative and comparative · as … as / the same as / similar to / different from

explanation.es:
Modificar comparativos

gran diferenciamuch / far / a lot biggerThe new flat is far bigger.
poca diferenciaa bit / slightly / a little cheaperIt's slightly cheaper online.
igualdad matizadanearly / not quite / just as … asIt's nearly as fast as the train.
multiplicartwice / three times as … asIt's twice as expensive as last year.

Estructuras especiales

The more you practise, the better you get. (cuanto más…, mejor…)
The sooner, the better.
It's getting hotter and hotter. Prices are more and more expensive. (cada vez más)

Igual, parecido, diferente

the same asMy phone is the same as yours.
similar toItalian is similar to Spanish.
different from (RU también to)British English is different from American English.
like / unlikeShe looks like her mother. Unlike me, he loves football.
✗ the same than → ✓ the same as · ✗ similar than → ✓ similar to · ✗ very bigger → ✓ much bigger · ✗ more and more big → ✓ bigger and bigger.
